proofs.proof_tex:
For each primitive interval, define the coverage events
\[
 E_0=\{q_0\in Q_0\},\qquad E_1=\{q_1\in Q_1\},\qquad
 E_s=\{s\in S\},\qquad E_c=\{c\in C\}.
\]
By the four marginal binomial assumptions and \(\mathrm{lem:clopper\text{-}pearson\text{-}exact\text{-}coverage}\),
\[
 \Pr_P(E_0^c)\leq\beta_0,\quad
 \Pr_P(E_1^c)\leq\beta_1,\quad
 \Pr_P(E_s^c)\leq\beta_s,\quad
 \Pr_P(E_c^c)\leq\beta_c.
\]
The pointwise indicator inequality
\[
 \mathbf 1_{(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)^c}
 \leq \mathbf 1_{E_0^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_1^c}
       +\mathbf 1_{E_s^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_c^c}
\]
and \(\mathrm{ass:confidence\text{-}budget}\) therefore give
\[
 \Pr_P(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)
 \geq 1-(\beta_0+\beta_1+\beta_s+\beta_c)\geq1-\beta.
\]
This is the union-bound argument and uses no joint-distribution or independence condition on the four counts.

Put \(E=E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c\).  On \(E\), validation transport gives \(v=s\in S\) and \(1-u=c\in C\).  Membership of \(P\) in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}\) gives the fixed channel-rectangle restrictions and \(v-u=d\geq\kappa\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{lem:assay\text{-}inversion}\) gives \(u\leq q_a\leq v\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Thus
\[
 (q_0,q_1,u,v)\in\widehat{\mathcal F}.
\]
For every \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), the compatible-root value at this true tuple consequently belongs to the image projected in \(\mathrm{def:confidence\text{-}projection}\).  By continuity and monotonicity in \(\theta\) from \(\mathrm{lem:root\text{-}comparative\text{-}statics}\), that true-channel image is
\[
 \{b_\theta(u,v):\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\}
 =[b_{\theta_U}(u,v),b_{\theta_L}(u,v)]=K^\star.
\]
Since \(I_\beta\) is the interval image over the larger projected domain, \(K^\star\subseteq I_\beta\) on \(E\).  The preceding probability bound is pointwise for every compatible \(P\); hence
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}
 \Pr_P\{K^\star\subseteq I_\beta\}\geq1-\beta.
\]
Neither this set-inclusion argument nor the union bound invokes uniqueness or differentiability of an optimizer, or positive dimension of a feasible face.  It therefore remains valid at optimizer ties, marginal contacts, and collapsed faces.

It remains to prove the asserted finite computation.  Write \(Q_a=[\ell_a,h_a]\), and define the closed validation rectangle in channel coordinates by
\[
 R_{uv}=\bigl([u_L,u_U]\cap\{1-c':c'\in C\}\bigr)
 \times\bigl([v_L,v_U]\cap S\bigr).
\]
A channel permits at least one pair \((\widetilde q_0,\widetilde q_1)\in Q_0\times Q_1\) satisfying \(u\leq\widetilde q_a\leq v\) if and only if it lies in
\[
 D_Q=R_{uv}\cap
 \{u\leq\min(h_0,h_1),\ v\geq\max(\ell_0,\ell_1),\ v-u\geq\kappa\}.
\]
Indeed, necessity follows from \(u\leq\widetilde q_a\leq h_a\) and \(v\geq\widetilde q_a\geq\ell_a\); conversely, these inequalities say that each pair of closed intervals \([\ell_a,h_a]\) and \([u,v]\) intersects, so a feasible \(\widetilde q_a\) can be chosen from that intersection.

Fix \((u,v)\in D_Q\).  The margin formulas in \(\mathrm{lem:assay\text{-}inversion}\), together with the monotonicities in \(\mathrm{lem:root\text{-}comparative\text{-}statics}\), give the exact profiles
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &\widetilde q_0&\widetilde q_1&\theta\\ \hline
 \text{lower endpoint}&\min(h_0,v)&\max(\ell_1,u)&\theta_U\\
 \text{upper endpoint}&\max(\ell_0,u)&\min(h_1,v)&\theta_L.
\end{array}
\]
For the lower endpoint, if the clipped polygon \(D_Q\cap\{v\leq h_0\}\) is nonempty, then the profile has \(p_0=1\); if \(D_Q\cap\{u\geq\ell_1\}\) is nonempty, it has \(p_1=0\).  In either case the support interval in \(\mathrm{lem:unique\text{-}compatible\text{-}root}\) forces \(b=0\), which is the global minimum because \(b\) is a probability.  Each nonemptiness question is a finite linear feasibility check.  If both clipped polygons are empty, then every point of \(D_Q\) has \(v>h_0\) and \(u<\ell_1\), and the lower profile fixes \((\widetilde q_0,\widetilde q_1)=(h_0,\ell_1)\).  After relabeling the endpoints of \(R_{uv}\) as the channel rectangle, this remaining domain is exactly a channel polygon of the form in \(\mathrm{def:channel\text{-}polygon}\).  The completeness part of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}sharp\text{-}envelope}\) therefore computes its minimum with the ten-point candidate map.

For the upper endpoint, split \(D_Q\) by the two lines \(u=\ell_0\) and \(v=h_1\).  On the resulting four closed polygonal regions, the profiled objective is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 u\leq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1
   &b_{\theta_L}(\ell_0,h_1;u,v)\\
 u\geq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1
   &(h_1-u)/(v-u)\\
 u\leq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1
   &(v-\ell_0)/(v-u)\\
 u\geq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1
   &1.
\end{array}
\]
The first identity is the nontrivial compatible-root region.  In the second region \(p_0=0\), so support compatibility forces \(b=p_1=(h_1-u)/(v-u)\).  In the third, \(p_1=1\), so it forces \(b=1-p_0=(v-\ell_0)/(v-u)\).  In the fourth, \((p_0,p_1)=(0,1)\), so \(b=1\).  The first region again has the channel-polygon form and is evaluated by the ten-point map; the fourth requires only a linear feasibility check.

On either fractional region, the denominator \(G(u,v)=v-u\) is affine and is at least \(\kappa>0\).  If \(z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i\) is a convex combination of the vertices of that region and \(N\) denotes its affine numerator, then
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{G(z)}
 =\sum_i
 \frac{\lambda_iG(z_i)}{\sum_k\lambda_kG(z_k)}
 \frac{N(z_i)}{G(z_i)}.
\]
The coefficients on the right are nonnegative and sum to one, so every value is a convex combination of vertex values.  Thus each fractional-region maximum occurs at a polygon vertex.  Shared boundaries may be included in both adjacent regions; deleting duplicates does not change the maximum.  This proves the stated four-region profiling rule, including all contacts and tied optimizers.

Finally consider \(\mathrm{def:kill\text{-}test\text{-}witness}\).  The lower profile uses
\[
 \widetilde q_0=0.4000678118,\qquad
 \widetilde q_1=0.3318863111,\qquad
 \theta=0.9016929770.
\]
The displayed channel \((u,v)=(0.0395824405,0.4886211008)\) lies in the stated calibration rectangle, obeys both margin inequalities, and satisfies
\[
 v-u=0.4490386603>0.4490386602=\kappa.
\]
It is therefore retained by the projected feasible set.  Direct substitution into \(\mathrm{def:compatible\text{-}root}\), using the stable quadratic form, gives
\[
 p_0=0.802793619282\ldots,\qquad
 p_1=0.650954798424\ldots,\qquad
 b=0.132058055576\ldots.
\]
For an exact decimal check, regard every displayed input as a terminating rational and let
\[
 F(x)=(\theta-1)x^2+\{1-(\theta-1)(p_1-p_0)\}x-p_1(1-p_0).
\]
Exact rational substitution yields
\[
 F(0.1320580555)<0<F(0.1320580556).
\]
The derivative \(F'(x)=2(\theta-1)x+1-(\theta-1)(p_1-p_0)\) is positive throughout the compatible support interval by the uniqueness argument in \(\mathrm{lem:unique\text{-}compatible\text{-}root}\).  Hence the unique root lies between those two decimals, and the lower projection retains \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed truncation precision.

We first establish a deterministic modulus.  Let \(\eta=(q_0,q_1,u,v)\) and \(\eta'=(q'_0,q'_1,u',v')\) be compatible primitive tuples, and fix \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\).  The segment joining them remains compatible because the channel rectangle, the inequalities \(u\leq q_a\leq v\), and the floor \(v-u\geq\kappa\) are linear.  Along this segment, \(d=v-u\geq\kappa>0\), and direct differentiation of
\[
 p_a=\frac{q_a-u}{v-u}
\]
gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial q_a}\right|=\frac1d,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial u}\right|
   =\frac{v-q_a}{d^2}=\frac{1-p_a}{d},
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial v}\right|
   =\frac{q_a-u}{d^2}=\frac{p_a}{d}.
\]
Compatibility gives \(0\leq p_a\leq1\), so all three absolute derivatives are at most \(1/\kappa\).  Segment integration therefore yields
\[
 |p_a(\eta)-p_a(\eta')|
 \leq\frac{|q_a-q'_a|+|u-u'|+|v-v'|}{\kappa}.
\]
The unit coordinatewise margin bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:root\text{-}comparative\text{-}statics}\), extended to boundary contacts by its continuity conclusion, now give
\[
 |b(\eta,\theta)-b(\eta',\theta)|
 \leq\frac{|q_0-q'_0|+|q_1-q'_1|
                  +2|u-u'|+2|v-v'|}{\kappa}.
\tag{1}
\]
Since \(|u-u'|=|c-c'|\) and \(|v-v'|=|s-s'|\), equation \((1)\) proves the asserted weights \((1,1,2,2)\) for the primitive coordinates \((q_0,q_1,s,c)\).

We next bound a Clopper--Pearson interval deterministically.  Suppose \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)\), let \(Q_\gamma(X)=[L_X,U_X]\) be its equal-tailed interval of total noncoverage \(\gamma\), and put
\[
 \varepsilon(N,\gamma)=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}}.
\]
For \(X<N\), its upper endpoint satisfies
\[
 \Pr_{U_X}\{X'\leq X\}=\gamma/2.
\]
Because \(U_X\geq X/N\), the lower-tail half of \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}binomial\text{-}deviation}\) implies
\[
 \frac\gamma2
 \leq\exp\{-2N(U_X-X/N)^2\},
\]
and hence \(U_X-X/N\leq\varepsilon(N,\gamma)\).  The case \(X=N\) has \(U_X=1=X/N\).  The symmetric upper-tail argument gives \(X/N-L_X\leq\varepsilon(N,\gamma)\), including \(X=0\), where \(L_X=0\).  Consequently, for every observation,
\[
 Q_\gamma(X)\subseteq
 [X/N-\varepsilon(N,\gamma),X/N+\varepsilon(N,\gamma)]\cap[0,1].
\tag{2}
\]

Index the four primitive probabilities by
\[
 (p_j^\star)_j=(q_0,q_1,s,c),\qquad
 (N_j)_j=(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0),\qquad
 (w_j)_j=(1,1,2,2),
\]
and set \(\varepsilon_j=\sqrt{\log(2/\beta_j)/(2N_j)}\).  On the simultaneous coverage event \(E\) constructed in \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}confidence\text{-}projection}\), the true and every projected value of primitive coordinate \(j\) lie in the same primitive interval.  By \((2)\), their distance is at most \(2\varepsilon_j\).  Applying \((1)\) to any projected tuple and the true tuple, for the same \(\theta\), gives
\[
 |b(\widetilde\eta,\theta)-b(\eta^\star,\theta)|
 \leq R,
 \qquad
 R=\frac2\kappa\sum_j w_j\varepsilon_j.
\tag{3}
\]
The true tuple is feasible on \(E\), so \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}confidence\text{-}projection}\) gives the first inclusion below.  As \(\theta\) varies, the true-root values fill \(K^\star\); taking the infimum and supremum over all projected tuples and \(\theta\) in \((3)\) gives the second inclusion:
\[
 K^\star\subseteq I_\beta
 \subseteq[\inf K^\star-R,\sup K^\star+R]\cap[0,1].
\]
The event has probability at least \(1-\beta\).  Only marginal tail bounds and the union bound were used, so mutual independence of the counts is unnecessary.

For the expectation assertion, let \(\widehat p_j\) be the four empirical proportions and define
\[
 R_{\mathrm{data}}
 =\frac1\kappa\sum_jw_j
   \bigl(|\widehat p_j-p_j^\star|+\varepsilon_j\bigr).
\]
The deterministic enclosure \((2)\) shows, without conditioning on coverage, that every projected value of coordinate \(j\) is within \(|\widehat p_j-p_j^\star|+\varepsilon_j\) of the truth.  Equation \((1)\) therefore places the entire projected root image inside the \(R_{\mathrm{data}}\)-enlargement of \(K^\star\).  Taking the interval image, and taking the length of an empty projection to be zero, yields
\[
 \{\operatorname{length}(I_\beta)-\operatorname{length}(K^\star)\}_+
 \leq2R_{\mathrm{data}}.
\tag{4}
\]
For each binomial empirical proportion, Cauchy--Schwarz and the binomial variance formula give
\[
 E_P|\widehat p_j-p_j^\star|
 \leq\sqrt{E_P(\widehat p_j-p_j^\star)^2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{p_j^\star(1-p_j^\star)}{N_j}}
 \leq\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}.
\]
Taking expectations in \((4)\) consequently gives the uniform bound
\[
 \sup_P E_P
 \{\operatorname{length}(I_\beta)-\operatorname{length}(K^\star)\}_+
 \leq\frac2\kappa\sum_jw_j
 \left\{\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}+\varepsilon_j\right\}
 =O\!\left(\frac1{\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}}\right),
\]
where the last equality uses fixed positive marginal budgets.  Every displayed constant is independent of the compatible primitive probabilities, which proves the stated uniformity.
